claims.statement: McDannald, Siderius, DeCost, Choudhary, Ortiz-Montalvo, Intrinsic Direct Air Capture, arXiv:2501.04825v1 (8 Jan 2025): idealised piston with three steps; E1 = Q_ads - W1 (eq. 1), E2 = integral over a path s in (T,P) space (eqs. 2-4), E3 = 0 'no energy recovery' (eq. 5), E_total = E1 + E2 + E3 (eq. 6), purity (eq. 7), xi = dn_CO2/E_total (eq. 8), C = 1/xi (eq. 9), optimisation prior (eq. 10: T1 >= 200 K, dT ~ U(0,200), P1 ~ U(101325, 1.1*101325), dP ~ U(-101225, 0)); Table 2 (14 Pareto rows, xi in umol/J, printed values 6.12 to 11.259); statements on pp. 14-15 (heat recovery 'could therefore exceed our stated upper limit') and p. 22 (T1 lower limit 200 K). The supplement was NOT read.

Dataset Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14452152 (NIST Data Publication 10.18434/mds2-3687, version 1.0; authors McDannald and Siderius; licence CC-BY-4.0) and code NIST IntrinsicDACCycle v0.0.2 (Julia, NIST software licence: use, copy, distribute and modify with the notice kept; modified works carry a change notice; NIST must be acknowledged as source). DAC_data.tar.gz md5 a2520f520140c60f8a4663d5b403966c equals the Zenodo value; sha256 75a73c75a376a4611511af4a9e99b15af10096fa1886e5d969e4a1d8268df3fa.

The sentence on p. 20 of arXiv:2501.04825v1 as extracted from the PDF text reads 'There are a few sorbents with intrinsic capture efficiencies above 1.0 x 10^5 mol/J for their Pareto optimal paths' (the exponent is printed without a minus sign in the extraction, while the next sentence's 2.46 x 10^-6 keeps its minus). The independent AI auditor rendered p. 20 at 150 dpi: the typeset PDF prints 1.0 x 10^5 mol/J with a positive exponent, so the positive exponent is in the typeset source; no person inspected the page.

Stylised two-component surrogate (van 't Hoff Henry loadings for CO2 and N2, sensible heat c = gamma R n0, heat-recovery fraction r on the sensible heat; code/cert_sign.py docstring): the benefit of starting at Tc < T0 instead of T0, beta = C(T0) - C(Tc), equals A + lam B + (1-r) gamma R D with A_ex = -(T0-Tc)(q_C/Tc - R) and A_fv = R(T0-Tc). Consequences by the Lean algebra: A_ex < 0 whenever q_C > R Tc; beta is affine in r, so r = 1 is the worst case for cold when D >= 0; at r = 1 cold wins iff lam B > -A_ex, i.e. (B > 0 and) lam > lam* = (T0-Tc)(q_C/Tc - R)/B; for r < 1 the heat-capacity threshold gamma > N/((1-r) R D) with N = -(A + lam B). The derivation of the decomposition from the surrogate's definition is a hand argument; only the algebraic steps are in Lean.

In the surrogate, A_ex < 0 over the whole parameter box Tc in [200,272] K, T0 in [273,313] K, Th in [315,400] K, q_C in [12,67] kJ/mol (certified; trivially, since q_C >= 12000 J/mol exceeds R*272 K = 2261 J/mol).

Certified signs of the surrogate benefit beta at the stated numeric parameters of 164 parameter sets (data/logs/surrogate_params.json) x 3 ambient temperatures x 3 recovery fractions (those with Tc < T0 only: 155, 159, 162 sets at T0 = 273.15, 298.15, 313.15 K): at T0 = 298.15 K and r = 0, 151 positive (cold wins), 8 negative, 0 undecided (159 sets); at T0 = 298.15 K and r = 1, 131 positive, 28 negative. Outward-rounded mpmath interval arithmetic; the statement is about the surrogate evaluated at those numbers.

An independent plain-float implementation of the surrogate lies inside the interval enclosures for 2854 of 2856 points; the other 2 differ by 3e-8 relative from float cancellation, with the same sign. The first run of the surrogate lacked the factor R on the sensible term (1904 of 2856 mismatches), was found by this check, fixed and rerun.

Positive control: the Python re-implementation of the published energy balance (code/k1/dac_model.py) with the dataset reproduces Table 2 in 14 of 14 rows, 8 of 8 printed fields each, from the stored posterior statistics (PC-a); recomputes every stored nominal array and E_total with maximum normalised deviation 3.755e-11 (PC-b; one density per material back-solved from one stored number); nominal versus posterior-mean xi differs by -2.3 % to +1.3 % (PC-c, unseeded 100-draw posterior); re-fitted Cv within 4.0e-6 relative (PC-d).

Exergy re-accounting of the 14 stored Table 2 paths at T0 = 298.15 K (heats weighted by Carnot factors, works kept at face value, Step 3 priced with the right-point rule of the published Step 2 (v2; v1 used a trapezoid; drift <= 2.4e-4 relative, no printed digit changes)): no-credit xi_NC (r = 0) 25.4 to 36.8 umol/J, against the face-value nominal recompute 5.98 to 11.26 umol/J (printed posterior means 6.12 to 11.259); reversible floor B_rev 25.0 to 27.0 kJ/mol against ideal-mixture W_min(P0, y) 18.8 to 19.4 kJ/mol (xi_rev 37.0 to 40.0 umol/J < 1/W_min); refrigeration is 47 to 80 % of the no-credit exergy cost. Sorbent heating is 1 to 45 % of the face-value E_total; the heats of adsorption plus desorption are 48 to 89 %.

Base accounting (feed air not priced, ideal machines), v2 joint grid plus refinement (T1 200 to 400 K incl. 2 K steps 270 to 298 K, T_end <= 400 K, P_end in [100, P1], 4,720 to 5,902 paths per row) of the 14 Table 2 rows: the exergy-optimal T1 lies in 200 to 236.75 K in 14 of 14 rows for every T0 in {273.15, 298.15, 313.15} K and r in {0, 0.5, 1}; 0 of 14 rows have T1* >= T0 in any variant; the face-value control puts all 14 optima below 273 K (maximum 232.1 K). Vacuity (all 14 rows): with the purity constraint on, no warm path (T1 >= T0) on the grid reaches the stored purity for any row at any T0, so the 9 constrained variants are vacuous for every row: 126 of 252 row-variants are informative (all unconstrained), not 252.

Base accounting, cold-start benefit ratio (best xi with T1 < 298.15 K / best xi with T1 >= 298.15 K, T0 = 298.15 K), 14 rows, v2 grid: face value 10.2 to 818; exergy r = 0: 3.5 to 129; r = 0.5: 2.6 to 79; r = 1: 1.29 to 6.6. Unconstrained optimal T_end: face value 230 to 400 K; exergy r = 0 301 to 340 K.

H2: over 8,765 materials with valid paths (15,161 paths; 11,656 optimised files in the public record), the published face-value xi never exceeds 1/W_min (dataset maximum 11.259 umol/J, VANNIK, against 51.6 umol/J). RETRACTION (v2): the v1 claim that five dataset entries (CSMNOX, GUSNEN, PACYIE, SABWAU01, UJOKIP05) have heat flows inconsistent with the second law is withdrawn. Rerun over all 15,161 paths, all three T0 and both W_min floors: with the v1 Step-3 trapezoid the G3 floor check flags 14/18/21 pairs (lowest-pressure floor; 3/5/7 materials) and 16/22/25 pairs (P0 floor; 63 in ten materials), reproducing v1 exactly; with the right-point rule of the published Step 2 it flags 0 at every T0 against both floors, and the G2 sensible closure holds to 4.4e-16. All flagged paths have dn_CO2 3e-9 to 3.4e-4 mol/kg and xi_fv 6e-8 to 2.9e-3 umol/J: the flags were a quadrature artefact amplified by tiny working capacities, not evidence about the entries. v1 also misprinted SABWAU01's B_rev (-41.9 kJ/mol, not J/mol) and called SABWAU01 and UJOKIP05 not degenerate (dn_CO2 4.2e-5 and 1.4e-4 mol/kg).

Slice scan on a seeded random sample of 150 materials (seed 20261027; best stored Pareto path of each; T_end, P1, P_end held): at T0 = 298.15 K and r = 0 the exergy optimum has T1* >= T0 in 3 of 150 (unconstrained). Re-selecting among all 15,161 stored Pareto paths of 8,765 materials, the no-credit-exergy-best path starts below 298.15 K for 8,420 of 8,765 materials (face value: 8,416). Conditional, not a re-optimisation.

Agreement of the surrogate sign (DAC-C-0003) with the full-model slice scan on the seeded 150-material sample at T0 = 298.15 K: 149/150 (r = 0), 146/150 (r = 0.5), 128/150 (r = 1). On the 14 Table 2 rows (paper-side recount, per path): r = 1 disagrees on 11 of 14 rows at T0 = 273.15 K, 10 of 13 scorable rows at 298.15 K and 5 of 8 at 313.15 K (the surrogate predicts cold loses; the full model says cold wins); at r = 0 all scorable rows agree. The interval statements are therefore about the surrogate only.

Controls: positive and negative. Positive: real BEVQID ledger passes the gate G1-G4; an all-T >= T0 path (min 300 K) has heat-in weights in (0,1), no refrigeration term, heat-out free; joint-scan face-value optimum reproduces 'start cold' (14/14 below 273 K); scan self-check <= 4.2e-7 relative. Negative, all rejected by the gate: double-counted sorbent heat (G2), planted x10^6 unit error (G4), the text's 1.0e5 mol/J taken literally (G4), heats of adsorption removed (G3: B_rev 8.73 kJ/mol < W_min 13.52 kJ/mol). All rerun under the v2 right-point Step-3 rule with the same outcomes. These plants test the gate, not the H1 conclusion; the H1 negative control is DAC-X-0014.

Unit observation: the dataset field Intrinsic_capture_efficiency carries the units string 'mol/J'; its maximum posterior value is 1.1259e-5 mol/J; 60 of the 8,765 materials have at least one path above 1.0e-5 mol/J; Table 2 prints xi in umol/J (maximum 11.259). The printed sentence (DAC-L-0003) is consistent with 1.0 x 10^-5 mol/J.

Neutral observations on the published code and data: unseeded 100-draw posterior; Cv drawn once per call so printed uncertainties omit Cv variability; Captured_CO2 is a posterior mean while E_Balance is nominal; three descriptions of the single path (text 250 to 350 K then 40,530 Pa; stored files and README 250 to 375 K and 42,844.84 Pa; code default 300 to 350 K); eight Table 2 rows with P1 in 82,466 to 101,126 Pa although eq. 10 and the v0.0.2 optimiser bound P1 to >= 101,325 Pa; nominal paths found by our grid with the published evaluator that exceed several Table 2 rows in both xi and purity (PARFOF 8.42 vs 5.98 umol/J at purity 0.99999; MAXHEA 8.62 vs 6.77; IFUDAO 8.60 vs 7.27), so the published front may not be fully converged (an observation to check, not a claim).

HEADLINE (v2, narrowed after the independent AI audit). In the published simplified model, for the 14 Table 2 rows: (a) with every heat of the sorbent and adsorbate Carnot-weighted at an explicit T0, Step 3 priced, works at face value, ideal machines and the feed air NOT priced, the exergy-optimal start stays at 200 to 236.75 K in 14/14 rows in all 9 informative variants (the 9 purity-constrained variants are vacuous), and the cold-start benefit shrinks (face value 10 to 818 -> r = 0 3.5 to 129 -> r = 1 1.29 to 6.6) but stays above 1; (b) with the chilling of the feed air priced (eps = 0, capture fraction 1, T0 = 298.15 K) a cold start still wins in 14/14 rows at r = 0 but at 254 to 288 K (ratio 1.46 to 8.0), and at r = 1 the optimum moves to ambient (297.25 to 297.75 K on a 0.25 K grid, advantage 0.07 to 0.35 %) in 11/14 rows; a start >= 10 K below ambient then loses unless eps > 0.91 to 0.96. H1 as preregistered (T1* >= T0 in > 50 % of rows at T0 = 298.15 K, r = 0) is refuted in both accountings (0/14); outside that setting the priced scenarios do not refute it for 11/14 rows at r = 1. The cold start's size, and at full recovery its existence, depend on how the feed-air chilling is priced. Thermodynamic limits of the published model only; the new scenario family is producer-computed, agrees with the auditor's numbers on 3 overlapping rows within stated tolerances, and awaits an independent re-check.

Absences recorded so they are explicit: the supplement of arXiv:2501.04825 was not obtained and not read; no human audit of this paper, code or Lean statements exists (the independent audit was by an AI agent; its report is AUDIT.md); the v2 feed-air scenario family, the H1 negative control and the full-record H2 rerun are not independently re-checked; the advisor review of the original K1 lane timed out; the repository guards (antigravity_guard.py, test_rigor_guard.py, pytest tests/) were not run; GATE-1 statement-adequacy checks were not run; no statement lock; no author contact was made. No output of any of these exists and none is claimed.

Feed-air scenario family (new in v2): n_air = dn_CO2 / x with x = 400e-6 (run_optimize_intrinsic_dac.jl:15; 2,500 mol air per mol CO2 at capture fraction f = 1, the case most favourable to a cold start), ideal chilling exergy n_air c_p [T0 ln(T0/T1) - (T0 - T1)] with c_p = 7/2 R, unrecovered share (1 - eps)/f added to B(r). At T0 = 298.15 K, eps = 0, ideal machines: r = 0 T1* 254 to 288 K, cold in 14/14; r = 0.5 T1* 268 to 290 K; r = 1 T1* at ambient (coarse grid: the 298.0 K cell; refined: 297.25 to 297.75 K, advantage over T1 >= T0 0.07 to 0.35 %) in 11/14 rows, VANNIK x2 (288 K) and LETQAE01 (284 K) cold for every eps. Recuperator threshold at r = 1 (cold = T1 <= T0 - 10 K): 0.91 to 0.96 in the 11 rows; auditor's split (T1 <= 290 K vs >= 298.15 K): 0.77 to 0.90. Machine sensitivity: refrigerator-only degradation without air flips r = 1 below eta_R 0.10 to 0.75; symmetric degradation without air strengthens the cold start in 14/14 rows. Agreement with the auditor (FASJAL 8.186, BEVQID 9.186, VANNIK 11.259): T1* within one grid cell, eta_R* at r = 1 within 0.015, eps* +0.04 and +0.09.

H1 negative control (new in v2): refrigeration costs (sorbent and feed air, eps = 0) multiplied by M, which cannot affect paths with T1 >= T0 and penalises every colder path. Through the same selection code, M = 1e4 is detected (T1* >= T0, ratio < 1) in 14/14 rows at r = 0, 0.5 and 1; M = 100 is detected in 7/14, 8/14 and 14/14 rows, the misses being the 298.0 K cell (refrigeration weight 5e-4). Sanity control: refrigeration and air free never make a cold start worse than in the base accounting (14/14 rows, all r).
